claims.claim: NVIDIA's FMS 2026 announcement blog defines SCADA as 'scaled, accelerated data access' and names no workload, no block size and no IOPS figure.
The shipping cuFile v1.18 API reference states that all cuFile APIs are issued from the CPU, not the GPU.
As of 2026-08-10 the XIO-SIG GitHub organisation contains only a placeholder .github repository; the four named projects (cuFile, cuFileConformance, libxFile, xioLinux) do not yet exist.
Kioxia's GP1 Series is rated up to 10 million random-read IOPS at a 512-byte block size, with evaluation samples available to select customers by the end of 2026.
The 100-million-IOPS figure is a forward-looking per-drive target for a future PCIe 7.0 generation, not a measured product; Kioxia's own 107 MIOPS demonstration ran on an emulation platform.
Micron's 230 million IOPS result is an aggregate across 44 Micron 9650 Gen6 SSDs at 512B, implying roughly 5.2M IOPS per drive.
Graid Technology reached 100 million random 512-byte IOPS on a RAID-5 protected volume built from 32 Kioxia XD8 SSDs — an array result, not a per-drive one.
The best shipping single-drive 4KB random read figure is 5.5M IOPS (Micron 9650, PCIe Gen6); Gen5 flagships cluster at 2.7-3.3M.
vLLM deliberately re-laid-out its KV cache so that one physical offload block spans all layers, growing it from a few KB to approximately 0.5-2 MB.
Llama-3.1-70B stores 327,680 bytes (320 KiB) of KV per token across all 80 layers: 2 x 80 x 8 x 128 x 2 bytes.
A 16-token vLLM block for Llama-3.1-70B is 5,242,880 bytes of KV, roughly ten thousand times a 512-byte I/O unit.
The BaM paper that underpins SCADA names graph and data analytics, recommender systems and graph neural networks as its motivating workloads; it predates the KV-cache era entirely.
At FMS 2026 Kioxia demonstrated 512-byte GP1 for 'near GPU workloads', context-memory caching on the CM9 TLC drive, and vector/RAG via AiSAQ — three separate products for three separate problems.
Meta's Bandana paper reports recommender embedding vectors of 64-128 bytes against a 4KB NVM block, wasting roughly 96% of read bandwidth.
The GIDS paper states GNN node feature sizes typically range from 512B to 4KB, and sizes the GPU cache line to the embedding to avoid I/O amplification.
NVIDIA's own KV-cache-on-flash proposal is CMX, a BlueField-4 Ethernet-attached G3.5 tier, whose materials never mention 512 bytes or IOPS.
NVIDIA's purpose-built massive-context inference GPU, Rubin CPX, solves the context-memory problem with 128GB of GDDR7, not flash.
Conventional DRAM contract prices rose approximately 93-98% quarter-on-quarter in 1Q26, lifting DRAM industry revenue 81% QoQ to $97 billion.
HBM per-wafer revenue was overtaken by DDR5 64GB RDIMM in 1Q26, inverting the assumption that HBM is the most profitable use of a DRAM wafer.
HBM took roughly 22% of top-three DRAM wafer input at end-2026 while producing only about 9% of DRAM bits.
Kioxia XL-FLASH is specified at under 5 microseconds read latency on a 128Gb SLC die with a 16-plane architecture — one to two orders of magnitude slower than DRAM's tens of nanoseconds.
A peer-reviewed IEEE Computer Architecture Letters analysis puts flash read energy at 102.4 pJ/bit against HBM3's 4.2 pJ/bit, a total path of 110.8 pJ/bit and roughly a 26-fold energy increase.
In a measured KV-offload deployment the flash tier ran at roughly 3.2 drive-writes-per-day against a 3 DWPD rating while using only about 1/28th of available bandwidth.
Samsung's own KV-cache-offloading white paper reports the NVMe configuration costing about 4% more below the crossover and reaching only 1.5x cost efficiency at 240 concurrent users.
A production KV-cache characterisation from Alibaba and SJTU concludes that a cache of 2x the per-GPU HBM approaches the ideal hit rate, eliminating the need for a CPU-RDMA-SSD storage hierarchy.
Mooncake's SSD offload is a July 2026 open-source feature benchmarked on a single 8xA100 node, not a disclosed Kimi production deployment.
Agentic coding traces show roughly 95.8% token-weighted prefix-cache hit rates, with misses clustering at gaps longer than five minutes.
Four major API providers price a cache hit at roughly 10% of uncached input tokens, and OpenAI and Anthropic now charge a write premium of 1.25x to 2x.
Intel began winding down the Optane memory business in Q2 2022, taking a $559 million inventory impairment.
PCI-SIG released the PCIe 7.0 specification at 128 GT/s on 2025-06-11, delivering up to 512 GB/s bidirectionally over x16.
Ten million IOPS at a 512-byte block size delivers 5.12 GB/s of payload bandwidth.
One hundred million IOPS at 512 bytes delivers 51.2 GB/s of payload, roughly 1/65th of an H100's 3.35 TB/s HBM bandwidth.
The first OCP High Bandwidth Flash specification defines three bandwidth grades from roughly 0.4 TB/s to 3.0 TB/s and up to 512GB per stack, and states no latency figure.
NAND contract prices rose 70-75% QoQ in 2Q26, outpacing conventional DRAM's 58-63%, with NOR flash and SLC NAND up more than 100% across the first half of 2026.
Memory rose from about 52% to about 63% of AI-chip component cost between Q1 2024 and Q4 2025, while advanced packaging fell from 19% to 15%.
Micron reported record FQ3 FY2026 revenue of $41.456 billion at 84.9% non-GAAP gross margin and guided FQ4 to $50 billion.
Analyst Jim Handy of Objective Analysis published a public rebuttal of the 100-million-IOPS SSD target, noting today's highest-performing SSDs deliver well under ten million IOPS.
Samsung's own scorecard records NVMe Zoned Namespaces as standardised but with low NVMe traction, because adoption requires major host-stack changes.
Kioxia's GP1 endurance rating is up to 50 DWPD, an unusually high figure that implies the vendor expects an extreme write load.
SanDisk reported FQ4 FY2026 revenue of $8.965 billion with datacenter revenue of $2.977 billion, roughly a third of the total.
